eye-chart.definition: A chart of letters or symbols viewed from a standard distance assesses how clearly a person can see.

phoropter.definition: An eye-examination instrument containing different lenses that an eye-care professional uses to compare visual corrections.
phoropter.exampleUsage: The optometrist changed lenses on the phoropter during the vision test.

slit-lamp.definition: A narrow, powerful beam of light lets an eye doctor examine the retina and optic nerve through a microscope.

retinoscope.definition: A hand-held eye instrument that shines light into the eye to help a clinician estimate refractive error.
retinoscope.exampleUsage: The eye doctor used a retinoscope during the examination.

tonometer.definition: Measuring instrument for measuring tension or pressure (especially for measuring intraocular pressure in testing for glaucoma).

ophthalmoscope.definition: Medical instrument for examining the retina of the eye.

pupil-dilation.definition: The pupil enlarges when light levels fall or shift, allowing more light to enter the eye.

visual-field.definition: The entire area visible to an unmoving eye at a particular moment.

refraction.definition: The change in direction of a propagating wave (light or sound) when passing from one medium to another.

cover-test.definition: An eye examination in which one eye is covered and then uncovered to assess how the eyes align and work together.
cover-test.exampleUsage: The clinician performed a cover test to check eye alignment.

autorefractor.definition: An electronic instrument that automatically estimates how the eye focuses light and helps measure refractive error.
autorefractor.exampleUsage: The autorefractor produced an initial estimate for the eye exam.

keratometer.definition: An instrument that measures the curvature of the front surface of the cornea.
keratometer.exampleUsage: The keratometer measured the corneal curvature.

perimeter.definition: The boundary line or the area immediately inside the boundary.

fundus-camera.definition: A specialized camera used to photograph the retina and other structures at the back of the eye.
fundus-camera.exampleUsage: The fundus camera captured an image of the retina.

oct-scanner.definition: An optical coherence tomography device that uses light to create detailed cross-sectional images of eye tissues.
oct-scanner.exampleUsage: The OCT scanner produced detailed retinal images.

biomicroscope.definition: A microscope used in eye care, often with a slit lamp, to examine structures at the front and sometimes back of the eye.
biomicroscope.exampleUsage: The clinician examined the cornea with a biomicroscope.

amsler-grid.definition: A grid of small squares lets people with age-related macular degeneration check their vision at home and notice changes.

ishihara-plates.definition: Printed color-dot plates used to screen for certain red-green color-vision deficiencies.
ishihara-plates.exampleUsage: The eye test included several Ishihara plates.

sunglasses.definition: (plural) spectacles that are darkened or polarized to protect the eyes from the glare of the sun.

contact-lens.definition: A thin, curved lens made of glass or plastic that rests on the cornea to improve vision or deliver medicine.

frame.definition: The supporting shape or structure of a building.

lens.definition: Biconvex transparent body situated behind the iris in the eye.

cleaning-cloth.definition: A soft cloth designed to clean lenses or delicate optical surfaces without scratching them.
cleaning-cloth.exampleUsage: She cleaned the glasses with a microfiber cleaning cloth.

nose-pad.definition: A small pad on eyeglass frames that rests against the side of the nose.
nose-pad.exampleUsage: The optician adjusted the nose pad for comfort.

temple.definition: The flat area on either side of the forehead.

hinge.definition: A circumstance upon which subsequent events depend.

bifocals.definition: (plural) eyeglasses having two focal lengths, one for near vision and the other for far vision.

progressive-lenses.definition: Eyeglass lenses with a gradual change in focusing power for viewing at different distances without visible dividing lines.
progressive-lenses.exampleUsage: The optician explained how progressive lenses contain several viewing zones.

reading-glasses.definition: Glasses designed mainly to help a person focus on nearby text or objects.
reading-glasses.exampleUsage: He uses reading glasses for small print.

safety-goggles.definition: Protective glasses worn to guard the eyes.

swimming-goggles.definition: Close-fitting protective eyewear designed to keep water away from the eyes while swimming.
swimming-goggles.exampleUsage: She wore swimming goggles in the pool.

anti-glare-coating.definition: A lens coating designed to reduce reflections and glare from the surfaces of eyeglasses.
anti-glare-coating.exampleUsage: The anti-glare coating reduced reflections on the lenses.

blue-light-glasses.definition: Glasses marketed with lenses that filter some blue wavelengths of light; evidence for broad health benefits is limited.
blue-light-glasses.exampleUsage: The optician explained that blue-light glasses filter some wavelengths but are not a cure for eye disease.

transition-lenses.definition: Photochromic eyeglass lenses that darken in brighter ultraviolet light and become clearer again indoors.

nearsighted.definition: Unable to see distant objects clearly.

astigmatism.definition: (ophthalmology) impaired eyesight resulting usually from irregular conformation of the cornea.

glaucoma.definition: An eye disease that damages the optic nerve and impairs vision (sometimes progressing to blindness).

cataract.definition: An eye disease that involves the clouding or opacification of the natural lens of the eye.

dry-eye.definition: Any felt dryness in the eye, including burning, grittiness, or the sense that something is present, whatever the cause.

color-blind.definition: Having a color-vision deficiency that makes some colors difficult to distinguish.
color-blind.exampleUsage: A person who is color blind may have difficulty distinguishing certain color combinations.

lazy-eye.definition: A common term for amblyopia, a condition in which vision in one eye does not develop normally during childhood.
lazy-eye.exampleUsage: The eye doctor explained that 'lazy eye' is another name for amblyopia.

crossed-eyes.definition: A common description of strabismus, in which the eyes do not point in the same direction at the same time.
crossed-eyes.exampleUsage: Crossed eyes can be a sign of strabismus that should be assessed by an eye professional.

floaters.definition: Spots before the eyes caused by opaque cell fragments in the vitreous humor and lens.

macular-degeneration.definition: This eye disease develops when cells in the macula lutea, the retina’s central area, deteriorate, causing blurred vision and sometimes blindness.

diabetic-retinopathy.definition: Damage to the retina’s small blood vessels can impair vision. Diabetic retinopathy develops when diabetes leaves blood glucose levels abnormally high over a long period, usually because the disease is poorly controlled.

conjunctivitis.definition: Inflammation of the conjunctiva of the eye.

stye.definition: An infection of the sebaceous gland of the eyelid.

corneal-ulcer.definition: An open sore or damaged area on the cornea, often related to infection or injury and requiring prompt professional assessment.
corneal-ulcer.exampleUsage: A suspected corneal ulcer needs prompt evaluation by an eye-care professional.

keratoconus.definition: Abnormal cone-shaped protrusion of the cornea of the eye.

presbyopia.definition: A reduced ability to focus on near objects caused by loss of elasticity of the crystalline lens after age 45.

retinal-detachment.definition: Vision loss occurs when the retina, the eye’s light-sensitive layer, separates from the choroid, the tissue beneath it, and doctors may treat it with laser photocoagulation.

amblyopia.definition: Visual impairment without apparent organic pathology.

prescription.definition: Available only with a doctor's written prescription.

eye-drops.definition: Sterile liquid medication or lubricant formulated to be placed in the eyes for a specific purpose.
eye-drops.exampleUsage: The patient used the eye drops only according to the label or clinician's directions.

laser-surgery.definition: A surgical procedure that uses a focused laser beam to treat tissue, including certain eye conditions.
laser-surgery.exampleUsage: The ophthalmologist discussed whether laser surgery was appropriate for the condition.

lens-implant.definition: A clear plastic lens inserted into the eye, usually after cataract surgery removes the eye’s natural lens.

patching.definition: The act of mending a hole in a garment by sewing a patch over it.

therapy.definition: (medicine) the act of caring for someone (as by medication or remedial training etc.).

medication.definition: (medicine) something that treats or prevents or alleviates the symptoms of disease.

dilation-drops.definition: Eye drops used by clinicians to temporarily enlarge the pupil for examination or certain procedures.
dilation-drops.exampleUsage: The clinician explained that dilation drops may temporarily blur near vision.

corrective-lens.definition: A lens in glasses or contact lenses designed to improve focus and correct refractive error.
corrective-lens.exampleUsage: The prescription specifies the power of the corrective lens.

prism.definition: Optical device having a triangular shape and made of glass or quartz.

lasik.definition: A refractive surgery procedure that reshapes the cornea, creating a corneal flap which contains both epithelial and deeper stromal tissues.

prk-surgery.definition: Photorefractive keratectomy, a laser eye procedure that reshapes the cornea to correct certain refractive errors.
prk-surgery.exampleUsage: The ophthalmologist explained the purpose and risks of PRK surgery.

cataract-surgery.definition: A surgeon removes the eye’s cloudy lens, or part of it, and replaces it with an intraocular lens, an artificial lens placed inside the eye.

intravitreal-injection.definition: A medical injection delivered by an eye specialist into the vitreous inside the eye to treat certain retinal conditions.
intravitreal-injection.exampleUsage: An intravitreal injection is performed by trained eye specialists under clinical conditions.

corneal-transplant.definition: A surgical operation replaces part or all of a damaged cornea, the eye’s clear front layer, with healthy tissue from a donor.

anti-vegf-therapy.definition: A treatment that blocks vascular endothelial growth factor and is used for certain retinal diseases involving abnormal blood vessels or swelling.
anti-vegf-therapy.exampleUsage: The retina specialist discussed anti-VEGF therapy as a treatment option.
anti-vegf-therapy.arabicTranslation: علاج مضاد لعامل نمو بطانة الأوعية (Anti-VEGF)

artificial-tears.definition: Lubricating eye drops designed to relieve dryness by supplementing the eye's natural tear film.
artificial-tears.exampleUsage: Artificial tears are lubricating drops for dry-eye symptoms; persistent symptoms should be assessed professionally.

warm-compress.definition: A clean warm cloth or pad placed over a body area for gentle warmth, including the eyelids in some eye-care routines.
warm-compress.exampleUsage: The clinician explained when a warm compress may be appropriate for eyelid care.

eye-patch.definition: A covering worn over one eye for protection or as part of treatment prescribed for certain conditions.
eye-patch.exampleUsage: The child wore the eye patch according to the eye specialist's plan.

vision-therapy.definition: A supervised program of visual activities prescribed for selected eye-movement, focusing, or binocular-vision problems.
vision-therapy.exampleUsage: The optometrist explained that vision therapy is appropriate only for certain diagnosed problems.

iris.definition: Muscular diaphragm that controls the size of the pupil which in turn controls the amount of light that enters the eye.

pupil.definition: The contractile aperture in the center of the iris of the eye.

cornea.definition: The transparent dome-shaped anterior portion of the outer covering of the eye.

retina.definition: The innermost light-sensitive membrane covering the back wall of the eyeball.

optic-nerve.definition: Each of two nerves carries visual signals from the retina to the brain; together, they form cranial nerve II.

eyelid.definition: Either of two folds of skin that can be moved to cover or open the eye.

eyelash.definition: Any of the short curved hairs that grow from the edges of the eyelids.

tear-duct.definition: A blocked tear duct prevents tears from draining into the nose, leaving the eyes unusually watery.

sclera.definition: The whitish fibrous membrane (albuginea) that with the cornea forms the outer covering and protection of the eyeball.

macula.definition: A cooler darker spot appearing periodically on the sun's photosphere.

vitreous-humor.definition: A clear, colorless gel fills the large cavity behind the lens inside the eyeball.

aqueous-humor.definition: A clear fluid fills the space inside the eye between the cornea at the front and the lens behind it.

ciliary-body.definition: A portion of the eye’s middle coat lies between the choroid, its vascular back layer, and the iris.

conjunctiva.definition: A transparent lubricating mucous membrane that covers the eyeball and the under surface of the eyelid.

choroid.definition: A highly vascular membrane in the eye between the retina and the sclera.

fovea.definition: Area consisting of a small depression in the retina containing cones and where vision is most acute.

blind-spot.definition: A small area of the retina lacks light-sensing cells where the optic nerve leaves the eye, causing a gap in your field of vision.

lacrimal-gland.definition: The gland above the outer part of each eye that produces much of the watery portion of tears.
lacrimal-gland.exampleUsage: The lacrimal gland helps produce tears.

waiting-room.definition: A room where patients sit until they are called for an eye-care appointment.
waiting-room.exampleUsage: Patients waited in the waiting room.

exam-chair.definition: An adjustable chair designed to support a patient during an eye examination.
exam-chair.exampleUsage: The patient sat in the exam chair.

display-wall.definition: A wall or panel used to present eyeglass frames, products, or information for patients to view.
display-wall.exampleUsage: The display wall held rows of eyeglass frames.

trial-frame.definition: An adjustable eyeglass-like frame used during an eye examination to hold different test lenses.
trial-frame.exampleUsage: The optometrist placed test lenses in the trial frame.

case-drawer.definition: A drawer used to store cases, small optical items, or examination accessories.
case-drawer.exampleUsage: The case drawer held empty eyeglass cases.

computer.definition: A machine for performing calculations automatically.

insurance-card.definition: A card or digital record that shows information about a person's health-insurance coverage.
insurance-card.exampleUsage: The adult patient showed an insurance card at reception.

appointment.definition: The act of putting a person into a non-elective position.

pre-testing-room.definition: A room where preliminary eye measurements and screening tests are performed before the main examination.
pre-testing-room.exampleUsage: The technician completed the initial measurements in the pre-testing room.

optical-dispensary.definition: An area where prescription eyeglasses and optical products are selected, fitted, adjusted, or collected.
optical-dispensary.exampleUsage: The patient chose new frames in the optical dispensary.

lens-edger.definition: A machine that cuts and shapes eyeglass lenses so they fit a particular frame.
lens-edger.exampleUsage: The lens edger shaped the lens to match the frame.

pupilometer.definition: An instrument used to measure the distance between the pupils, often for fitting eyeglass lenses.
pupilometer.exampleUsage: The optician used a pupilometer before ordering the lenses.

lensometer.definition: An optical instrument used to measure the prescription power and other properties of eyeglass lenses.
lensometer.exampleUsage: The lensometer confirmed the power of the existing glasses.

frame-display.definition: A stand, shelf, or panel used to show eyeglass frames.
frame-display.exampleUsage: The frame display included several shapes and sizes.

adjustment-tools.definition: Small tools used by an optician to fit, tighten, align, or repair eyeglass frames.
adjustment-tools.exampleUsage: The optician kept adjustment tools beside the fitting desk.

ultrasonic-cleaner.definition: A cleaning device that uses high-frequency sound waves in a liquid to remove dirt from small objects.
ultrasonic-cleaner.exampleUsage: The ultrasonic cleaner was used for compatible optical parts.
